editorial.tldr: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 launched in late July under a US distillation dispute and a chip-export claim, as Moonshot's own valuation kept climbing toward a Hong Kong IPO. DeepSeek then shifted the fight from models to agent tooling, open-sourcing an agent framework built to challenge Claude Cowork directly.
editorial.whats_new: DeepSeek's open-source Harness, pitched against Claude Cowork, picked up a third independent MIT-license confirmation on Aug 17 — this one framing it as a tool for AI coding agents — with still no published v0.1 changelog.
editorial.why_it_matters: Harness gives platform engineers an MIT-licensed, now triple-sourced agent-orchestration layer they can pin to a specific version, but the unbenchmarked 'beats Claude Code' claim and the missing v0.1 changelog mean it isn't yet a drop-in Cowork/Code replacement.
editorial.take_for_builders: Pilot DeepSeek's MIT-licensed Harness against Claude Cowork/Code before committing to an agent-tooling stack — the license is now independently confirmed by three outlets — but treat 36Kr's 'beats Claude Code' claim as unverified until an independent benchmark confirms it, and hold off pinning a version until v0.1 ships release notes.

status.state: DeepSeek's Harness reaches v0.1, pitched against Claude Cowork
status.detail: DeepSeek open-sourced Harness on Aug 13 as its answer to Claude Cowork, drew a contested 36Kr claim that it beats Claude Code on agentic tasks, reached a versioned v0.1 release on Aug 17, and picked up a third independent MIT-license confirmation the same day — still with no published changelog.
